title: Edmund and the Bridge
premise: In the winter of 1747, Odile Brightwater keeps the lighthouse at Greyhaven Point and grieves quietly for a husband lost to the sea. When a smuggler's boat leaves a mute child named Edmund on her doorstep with a sealed packet and one instruction — forget the face — she recognizes the boy as the son of a man who once saved her life. The packet holds proof that a respected magistrate orchestrated the wreck that killed her husband, and three fortified checkpoints stand between her and the assize court across the frozen river. Smuggling Edmund and the evidence north before the ice breaks, Odile finds an unlikely found family among ferrymen, nuns, and river folk, until loyalty to old debts collides with the truth she owes the living. At the bridge as it cracks apart in the thaw, she must choose between destroying the evidence to save Edmund or delivering it and avenging the dead; she delivers it, the magistrate falls, and she and Edmund keep the light together.
about_author: Sable Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal shipping records and coroner's inquests from the eighteenth century. They write historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of official silence.

chapters.title: The Lamp Room
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Establishes her widowed routine: trimming wicks, logging weather, speaking mostly to gulls. A letter arrives announcing the year's first great storm. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a coat, and the small pride of competence.

chapters.title: A Knock at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During the storm's aftermath she finds a boy asleep against her door with a wax-sealed packet tucked in his coat and no note but 'forget the face.' He does not speak. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Packet Holds
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She breaks the seal despite herself: manifests, a bribe ledger, and initials matching Magistrate Corven Hale — the man whose court condemned the ship her husband served on. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: Edmund
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, sparse and watchful. Flashbacks in fragments: a burning warehouse, his father's hand, a whispered instruction. He tests whether Odile can be trusted by hiding the ledger page he tore out. Emotional beat: a child deciding whom to love.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The tollhouse at Millbeck Bridge, where a bored sergeant searches carts for 'seditious papers.' Odile hides the packet inside a hollowed lamp-oil flask. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into craft.

chapters.title: Old Debts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She visits Tobias Finch, a retired ferryman who owed her husband his life, and asks him to move them upriver. He refuses — then sees Edmund's face and goes pale. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Hale's Men
chapters.summary: Sergeant Rook's POV. Corven Hale's enforcer arrives at Millbeck with a description of a woman and child and orders to burn what they find. Rook, uneasy, begins to wonder what he's actually hunting. Emotional beat: a henchman's first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: The Convent at Ashford Sluice
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Sheltered by nuns, Odile learns Edmund's father was a customs informer against Hale. Sister Verity offers to hide the boy permanently. Emotional beat: the temptation to stop running and let someone else carry it.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He finally gives Odile the page he hid — his father's dying confession naming Hale outright. Trust is made explicit. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes load-bearing.

chapters.title: Rook Closes In
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Following the oil-flask trick backwards, Rook traces them toward Ashford. He warns a nun instead of reporting her, choosing a small treason. Emotional beat: conscience outweighing career.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Marsh
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A night crossing of the fen with Finch's cousin, pursued by lantern-light. Edmund nearly drowns in a drain-cut; Odile pulls him out. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce maternal certainty.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. He agrees to run them past the second checkpoint at Weir Lock but names his price: Odile testifies not just against Hale but against the harbor board that let ships rot. Loyalty vs. truth turns inward. Emotional beat: complicity examined.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: Weir Lock
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hidden beneath eel baskets while Rook's men walk the lock gates inches above her head. Edmund, playing a deaf fisher-boy, distracts a corporal. Emotional beat: held breath, then wild relief.

chapters.title: Ice Voices
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Waiting at a drover's inn, Edmund speaks aloud for the first time since his father's death — a single sentence about the fire. Odile answers with her own confession about her husband. Emotional beat: two broken people becoming family.

chapters.title: The Trap at Harrow Bend
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Ordered to ambush the road north, Rook deliberately misroutes his men, buying the fugitives a day. His subordinate grows suspicious. Emotional beat: a man burning his own ladder behind him.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Drover's Inn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An ostler sells their route to Hale's men; they flee through the stable yard under gunfire, the packet scorched at its edge. Finch takes a graze. Emotional beat: trust wounded but not killed.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The fortified bridge at Stonecross, where the assize clerk demands papers and reads faces. Odile presents herself openly as a lighthouse keeper escorting a ward to kin — the boldest lie yet. Emotional beat: courage as performance.

chapters.title: Corven Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. In his study, Hale burns correspondence and reflects on the wrecks he purchased, including the one that took Brightwater. He learns the packet survived. Emotional beat: cold vanity beginning to sweat.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks Early
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The thaw comes ahead of schedule; Stonecross bridge groans, and the assizes sit across a river turning lethal. Finch rigs a rope ferry. Edmund refuses to be left behind. Emotional beat: the deadline arriving like a verdict.

chapters.title: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. Mid-crossing, Rook — now openly turned — holds off Hale's riders as the ice splits. Odile nearly drops the packet into the flood and must choose between saving it and saving Edmund, who has gone back for it. Both survive; the evidence reaches the courthouse steps as the bridge collapses behind them. Emotional beat: everything risked, everything answered.

chapters.title: The Assize
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Testimony, cross-examination, Hale's ledger read aloud. Rook corroborates at cost to himself. Hale is convicted; the harbor board trembles. Emotional beat: quiet vindication, grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Keeping the Light
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, resolution. Spring at Greyhaven Point: Edmund logs the weather in a careful child's hand, Finch visits with eels and gossip, and the lamp burns for ships that come home. Emotional beat: found family anchored, the past honored and finally at rest.
